comment:purpose: The SHIPPED ingest profile: the closed x_domain and type vocabularies plus the mechanical path→label tables. Data only — the resolution mechanism (longest-prefix-wins, segment-rule override, write-time rejection of an unknown label) lives in src/ingestProfile.ts and does not change with this file.
comment:editing: An unknown domain or type is REFUSED at write time, so a new label MUST be added to `domains`/`types` here before any rule may name it. A missing or malformed file is a hard error — ingest MUST NOT fall back to built-in values. The shipped vocabularies are mirrored as TypeScript unions in src/config.ts and the two are checked equal at load, so a value added here MUST be added there too.
name: default
comment:types: `knowledge` is the FALLBACK, not the norm — the directory an authored document lives in already carries what kind of document it is, so it stays for the sources no rule claims. `research`, `plan` and `lessons-learned` are accepted on write but deliberately claimed by NO rule: their real directory names are not settled, and a guessed prefix mislabels silently.
comment:domainRules: Order is PRESENTATION only (narrow roots first, for reading); resolution sorts by prefix length, so `claude-artifacts/` catches everything `claude-artifacts/standards/` does not, and `doc/` everything the ADR root does not. `dp-gnosis/cache/bench/corpus-ext/` is a BENCHMARK corpus root holding other projects' published docs, not product knowledge.
comment:typeRules: Same longest-prefix-wins rule: `doc/40-code-standards/90-decisions/` (adr) outranks `doc/40-code-standards/` (standard) by prefix length, not by row order. The external benchmark root types as `vendor-doc` so a type filter alone separates it from authored repo knowledge.
comment:excludePaths: `docs/` holds 22,808 .md files, and 22,597 of them are machine output: `docs/tmp` (12,211) and `docs/benchmarks` (10,386). Ingesting them buries the ~211 authored documents that are the actual target, so the two generated roots are excluded by path before anything is chunked. Same prefix semantics as domainRules: a repo-relative, forward-slash prefix.
comment:defaultExcludedTypes: Owner decision D5, 2026-08-18: 6,475 of 11,345 atoms (57.1%) are history-shaped — a feature log, a benchmark run, a review or a brainstorm — and on the CLI path they drown the authored knowledge a question is asking for. They stay INGESTED and INDEXED and are one flag away; only the default result set leaves them out, so the benchmark still measures the FULL corpus and every recorded number stands. Nothing reads this key yet — the CLI wiring is a separate task.
comment:segmentRules: Brainstorms are a SEGMENT rule, not a prefix rule: the directory appears under three unrelated parents, and enumerating those parents would silently mislabel the fourth one somebody adds. Matched on whole path segments, so a directory merely ENDING in the name cannot claim it. A segment rule OVERRIDES every prefix rule.
